8.title: EMAIL 8 – Bonjour from Bordeaux
8.subject: Bonjour from Bordeaux · A small table by the river ·
body: Bonjour,

A small table outside a café in Bordeaux, late afternoon. A tram glides past on the Cours de l'Intendance — silent, no overhead wires, only a faint electric hum and the brush of pale stone facades reflected in its windows.
The kind of small moment a French Atelier session is built around.
The waiter steps over. He doesn't rush.
— Vous prenez un verre ?— Un verre de rouge, s'il vous plaît. Quelque chose d'ici.
— Bien sûr.
A few minutes later, a glass arrives. He lingers, tells you a little about it, asks where you've come from.
You answer in three words. He nods, refills the carafe of water, moves on.
That's the shape of French here — a few clear words at the right time, and a doorway opens. To a person, to a place, to an afternoon you'll remember in French.
Step into a real exchange → bonjour-from-bordeaux.pplx.app

10.title: Email 10 – French Alps (Immersive Journey continues)
10.subject: Email 10 – French Alps (Immersive Journey continues)
body: Subject line: Une fondue, s'il vous plaît · A small table in the mountains ·
Bonjour,
You leave the coast behind. The train climbs. By late afternoon, the air is colder, thinner, and the light has turned the kind of blue that only happens above 1,500 metres.
The kind of small moment a French Atelier session is built around.
A small chalet-restaurant in Chamonix, just off the slopes. Wooden walls, the smell of melted cheese, snow boots drying by the door. The waiter looks up.
— Bonjour. Une fondue savoyarde pour deux, s'il vous plaît.— Avec un peu de vin blanc à côté ?— Volontiers.

A few minutes later, the caquelon arrives — bubbling, warm, faintly nutty. The bread cubes go in slowly. Celui qui perd son pain donne une tournée, the waiter says with a small smile. The one who loses their bread buys the next round.
You answer in three words. The mountain settles around the table.
Step into the next moment → https://bonjour-from-chamonix.pplx.app

11.title: Email 11 — Bonjour from Champagne
11.subject: Une coupe de blanc de blancs · A small moment among the vines ·
body: Bonjour,
You leave the mountains behind. The train slips north through low green hills, and by mid-afternoon you are walking between rows of chalk-pale vines stretching out toward Reims.
You don't need a tour. You need a few words, used at the right moment. That is what a French Atelier session is for.
A small family domaine off the route touristique, just past the village of Hautvillers. A wooden door, a slate sign, three stools at a counter. The vigneronne wipes her hands on her apron.
— Bonjour. On peut goûter ?
— Bien sûr. On commence par le blanc de blancs ?
— Volontiers.
The first sip is fine, dry, slightly chalky — the soil speaking before she does. On dit que c'est la craie qui parle, she says. They say it's the chalk that speaks.
La craie qui parle, you repeat. She nods, pleased, and pours a second. The afternoon settles around the counter.
Step into the next moment →  https://bonjour-from-champagne.pplx.app

12.title: Email 12 – Paris (Grand Finale – Immersive Journey)
12.subject: Comme d'habitude · A small return to where it began ·
body: Bonjour,
You've come back. The light is grey-blue, the rooftops are zinc, and the city smells faintly of rain on stone. After Nice, Bordeaux, Chamonix, Champagne — Paris feels narrower, quicker, more itself.
A small café on a side street in the 11th. Two tables outside, one inside near the bar. The waiter recognises no one and everyone at the same time.
— Bonjour. Un café, s'il vouLeave s plaît.
— Comme d'habitude ?
— Oui, merci.

He nods and turns to the machine. The machine hisses, the cup is rinsed, the grounds tamped slowly. The cup arrives, the saucer arrives, the small spoon arrives. Comme d'habitude — the usual — three words that mean you've been here before, even if it's the first time.
Outside, a woman folds her umbrella. Someone whistles a tune from across the street. Paris doesn't perform for you anymore. It just lets you in.
Step into the next moment → bonjour-from-paris.pplx.app

7.title: Email 7 — Real Life France 2.0
7.subject: Email 7 — Real Life France 2.0
body: Subject line: 3 simple French phrases for the boulangerie
It's just past eight. The bakery smells of warm butter and crust. The woman behind the counter looks up — and you only need three sentences.
"Bonjour, une baguette, s'il vous plaît." - Hello, one baguette, please.
"Et deux croissants." - And two croissants.
"Je peux payer par carte ?" Can I pay by card?
That's it. Three small phrases, and the moment carries itself. The baker nods. You step out with a paper bag still warm in your hand.
This is what we mean by real-life French. Not perfect grammar. Not memorized vocabulary. Just the right phrases for the right moment, said calmly, in context.
No fluency required. No tourist clichés. Just the small French moments you could actually handle.
See more situations like this → https://real-life-france-2.pplx.app/

9.title: Email 9 – Mediterranean Coast (Immersive experience)
9.subject: Email 9 – Mediterranean Coast (Immersive experience)
body: Subject line: Une glace, s'il vous plaît · A small moment by the sea ·
Bonjour,
A long staircase down to the Promenade des Anglais. Late June, late afternoon — the kind of light that turns Nice's pebbles a pale gold and softens every voice on the shore.
The kind of small moment a French Atelier session is built around.
You stop at a small glacier near the Place Masséna. The vendor leans on the counter, the coloured tubs lined up behind him.
— Bonjour. Une boule, citron-basilic, s'il vous plaît.— En cornet ou en pot ?— En cornet. Merci.
He hands it over with a small bonne dégustation.

You walk back toward the sea. Two teenagers on the rocks rehearsing a line from a film. A woman closing her parasol against the wind. Nothing performed, nothing translated. Just one short exchange, and a place that lets you in.
Step into a real exchange → https://bonjour-from-nice.pplx.app/

body: Subject line: Bienvenue. You're in the right place.

2.title: Email 2 — How it Works
2.subject: Email 2 — How it Works
body: Subject line: Here's how French Atelier actually works
Bonjour,
A quick note to make things clear, because we know "online French" can mean a lot of different things.

French Atelier isn't an app, and it isn't a stack of videos to watch alone. It's a real, culture-focused and structured course — streamed live from beautiful French locations and delivered in small groups by a native French teacher who guides every session.

You'll meet weekly for around five months. Each session has a clear shape, planned ahead of time. You don't need to prepare alone. You don't try to figure out what comes next. The path is laid out for you, step by step.
Everything else — class recordings, notes, places to ask questions — sits quietly in one platform you can return to whenever you'd like. And whenever you want to talk to us, we are one click away.
It's simple by design — and you're in good hands.
See how it works → /how-it-works
Until soon,

3.title: Email 3 — You’re not starting from zero
3.subject: Email 3 — You’re not starting from zero
body: Subject line: You already know more French than you think
Bonjour,
A quick, kind reminder before anything else: you're not starting from zero.

If you've ever said bonjour, merci, or au revoir, you've already begun. A few words, a song you half-remember, a menu you once read in a café — all of it counts. French isn't a door you're locked out of. It's a room you've already glanced into.

At French Atelier, we begin from where you are. Not from a perfect score, not from a placement test that makes you feel small. From a real first conversation, gentle and clear, in a small group with a teacher who's listening.
Progress here happens step by step. One word becomes one sentence. One lesson becomes a small habit. Nothing rushed, nothing skipped, nothing assumed.
You begin where you are. We walk with you from there.
See where you might begin → https://you-are-not-starting-from-zero.pplx.app/
Until soon,

4.title: Email 4 — You’re not starting from zero
4.subject: Email 4 — You’re not starting from zero
body: Subject line: Un café, s'il vous plaît · A small moment, in French ·
Bonjour,
Imagine a small café in a quiet neighborhood — not on a postcard, just on a regular Tuesday morning.
You step in. The barista glances up.— Bonjour.— Bonjour. Un café, s'il vous plaît.— Tout de suite.
Three short lines. The whole exchange takes less than a minute. You sit by the window with a small white cup, a sugar cube, the soft clink of someone else's spoon.

That's what French often looks like, day to day. Not a long performance. It's also the French we teach - a few clear words at the right moment, and a small space opens up — between you and a place, between you and a person.
This is what we mean by culture speaks French. Not the idea of France. The texture of an ordinary day there.
Step into a real moment → real-life-france.pplx.app
Until soon,

5.title: Email 5 — Content + gentle transition
5.subject: Email 5 — Content + gentle transition
body: Subject line: Learn just 3 phrases for a glass of Bordeaux
Bonjour,

Here's something small and useful thay you may learn during one of our French classes — three short phrases for a moment you might really live one day, in a Bordeaux cellar, in front of a bottle of red.
— Un verre de rouge, s'il vous plaît.(A glass of red, please.)
— Qu'est-ce que vous me conseillez ?(What would you recommend?)
— À votre santé.(To your health — said before the first sip.)
Three phrases. Enough to be welcomed not as a tourist, but as someone who came to taste, and to understand a little.
Bordeaux is built on these moments — quiet cellars, oak barrels, a small glass placed in front of you. The French word for them is dégustation: to taste, slowly, with attention.
If you want, see how a small phrase becomes a real moment → https://a-small-taste-of-french.pplx.app
Until soon,
